prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: one high-fidelity portrait mobile web app screen, a 390 × 844 smartphone viewport, approximately 9:19.5 aspect ratio
Primary request: Design a shippable mobile-first interface for an interactive browser latte art simulator called LatteArt. This must read unmistakably as a functional product UI, not a poster, photograph, editorial layout, or concept-art scene.
Surface structure, top to bottom: a compact 56 px top bar; a dominant central work area with one very large round latte canvas; a quiet compact action row; a three-control thumb-reach tool dock; and a thin collapsed advanced-settings drawer at the bottom. Preserve generous breathing room while fitting the entire interface in one viewport.
Top bar: “LatteArt” at left in refined humanist sans typography. At right, a compact “繁中 / EN” language control followed by one small settings button using a crisp custom line icon, no glyph or emoji.
Central simulator: one large perfectly round cup/canvas, about 300 px across, centered and clearly interactive. It is shown from directly overhead with a tactile off-white rough-stoneware rim, subtle realistic depth, and a deep espresso surface containing a beautiful but actively editable cream-and-coffee rosetta swirl. Add a restrained interaction cue within the canvas—a small precise circular tool point and a faint short flow trace—so it reads as a live simulator rather than a decorative beverage photo. The cup sits in a shallow celadon-glaze recessed work well integrated into the UI.
Action row: one understated secondary “Reset” control, clearly tappable but subordinate.
Thumb-zone controls: three immediately available, equal-width large tactile buttons labeled exactly “Pour”, “Stir”, and “Lift”. Use consistent authored line icons: a tiny pouring vessel for Pour, a circular stirring motion for Stir, and a lifted droplet for Lift. Make Pour the selected state with a dark blue-green glaze fill and light lettering; Stir and Lift are pale celadon ceramic surfaces with dark lettering. Minimum visual touch targets around 52 px. These are UI controls, not sample tiles.
Collapsed advanced settings: a thin bottom drawer lip with a centered tactile handle and one small sliders line icon only, visibly closed; show no settings fields and no extra label.
Visual world: mature, restful ceramic glaze test studio. Dominant move is the cup treated like an unfinished glaze specimen on a crafted test bench. Blue-green charcoal #21343B, muted celadon #6F8F83, pale celadon #D7E0D6, kiln-paper cream #F5F1E8, restrained fired terracotta #9D5D45. Materials are subtle blue-gray glaze, rough ceramic edges, and lightly debossed paper-label details. Sophisticated, calm, tactile, contemporary, handcrafted without rustic kitsch. Soft directional studio light, low broad shadows with real offset and blur, precise spacing, high contrast, refined restrained texture. Avoid generic glossy SaaS cards; use ceramic slab seams and glaze-edge variation as the component grammar. Rounded corners are moderate, not pill-shaped except the compact language control.
Text (verbatim, and no other visible words): “LatteArt”, “Pour”, “Stir”, “Lift”, “Reset”, “繁中 / EN”
Typography: render every listed string exactly once, clean and fully legible; no decorative microcopy, numbers, tooltips, headings, slogans, or placeholder text.
Constraints: single full-bleed UI screen only; no phone or device frame; no hands; no surrounding room; no status bar; no watermark; no logo mark; no emoji; no Unicode glyphs used as icons; no childish colors; no neon; no gradient text; no glassmorphism; no photographic background; no invented claims; no extra controls; no illegible decorative copy. The large round latte canvas must remain the unmistakable focal point and all three primary tools must be immediately visible in thumb reach.
